brief: GS's US morning update covers several desk views. On credit, Lynam argues rising rate volatility would cut IG/HY demand and widen spreads. If growth stays firm, credit absorbs higher rates fine and may even draw buyers, but if sovereign risk or inflation drive rates up instead, spreads get pressured. On oil, Grigsby notes Persian Gulf exports have recovered to 2025 levels yet Brent stays elevated. She attributes this to non-OECD visible stocks falling near record lows, which tightens pricing and spurs restocking. Brent also carries a near-record geopolitical risk premium that could keep prices above fair value if diplomatic tensions persist. Energy analysts favor Buy-rated COP, OXY, PR, PWR, BKR, GLNG, DINO, VLO, MPC, TRP and AR into Q4, staying constructive on refining with upside to consensus. A consumer note says inflation is squeezing lower-income spending flexibility, but overall credit health stays constructive on low unemployment and stable delinquencies. It forecasts 2027 discretionary cash-flow gains across income quintiles with the lowest-income cohort lagging, favoring FICO, DKS, ULTA and other staples names. GS downgraded Asahi Kasei to Neutral and Mitsui Chemicals to Sell. UMich sentiment is forecast at 47.0, below the 47.7 consensus and 48.1 prior reading.
